thesis: Test whether a 1-bit residual correction composes orthogonally with nsep+pchan, and whether a per-channel RMS magnitude is essential for Mode 1 models.

nsep+pchan INT2 + R-0.25.note: WORSE than INT2 alone; fixed magnitude backfires

nsep+pchan INT3 + R-0.25.note: WORSE than INT3 alone; fixed backfires here too

finding_1_rms_essential_for_mode1.observation: Fixed-magnitude 0.25 residual BACKFIRES on Mode 1 (Qwen2-7B): INT2+0.25 is +463 (worse than INT2 alone +326), INT3+0.25 is +0.89 (worse than INT3 alone +0.40).
finding_1_rms_essential_for_mode1.mechanism: Mode 1's outlier-driven residual distribution is heavily non-uniform; the E[|residual|] = 0.25 uniform-assumption constant is wrong. Per-channel RMS adapts: small on smooth channels, large on outlier channels.
finding_1_rms_essential_for_mode1.implication: Residual correction MUST use per-channel RMS (or similar adaptive magnitude) on Mode 1 models. Fixed constants harm.

finding_2_int3_rms_beats_int4_alone.observation: Qwen2-7B nsep+pchan INT3 + RMS residual: ΔPPL +0.025 at 4+D/head bits, surpassing native INT4 alone (+0.054) by 2.2x precision.
finding_2_int3_rms_beats_int4_alone.interpretation: A new Pareto-optimal point on Mode 1: the per-channel RMS residual captures outlier-correlated error that per-row absmax INT4 cannot.
finding_2_int3_rms_beats_int4_alone.caveat: D/head bits of per-channel RMS scale is a small metadata overhead (128 FP16 per head, ~256 bytes). Not free but negligible at scale.

finding_3_mode2_insensitive_to_magnitude.observation: On Llama (Mode 2), fixed-0.25 and RMS-per-channel produce near-identical results: both INT3+residual reach +0.075.
finding_3_mode2_insensitive_to_magnitude.interpretation: Mode 2's residual distribution is approximately uniform (no outlier bias). The magnitude choice doesn't matter much; any reasonable constant works.
finding_3_mode2_insensitive_to_magnitude.implication: For Mode 2 deployment, the simpler Fixed-0.25 residual suffices. For Mode 1, RMS is essential.

finding_4_int2_plus_residual_does_not_be.observation: At 3-effective-bit budget: INT3 alone wins. INT2+RMS is close (+0.47 vs +0.40 on Qwen) but does not surpass. On Llama the gap is larger (+0.71 vs +0.27).
finding_4_int2_plus_residual_does_not_be.interpretation: Dropping a bit in the base quantizer and gaining it back via residual is not uniformly beneficial. INT3's cleaner levels beat INT2's looser + 1-bit correction.
finding_4_int2_plus_residual_does_not_be.implication: The sweet spot remains INT3 for pure-quality and INT3+RMS for quality-at-any-cost.

composition_implications.modeq_extension_candidate: Add nsep+pchan+residual variant to the library (v0.2). The RMS per-channel variant is recommended default; fixed-0.25 should be discouraged on unaudited models.
composition_implications.nsn_contribution: Residual correction as orthogonal composition: provides a new Pareto-optimal point on Mode 1 at 4+ε bits, surpassing native INT4. Complements (does not compete with) TurboQuant's rotated QJL residual.
composition_implications.relationship_to_turboquant: TurboQuant's 1-bit residual operates on post-rotation scalar quantization of the full vector. Ours operates on per-channel absmax-scaled direction values of normalized vectors. Mechanistically orthogonal axes; both address residual quantization error, via different bases.

open_questions: Does RMS residual generalize to all 7 models from Phase 4, not just Qwen2-7B and Llama?
Can real bit-packing implement the 1-bit sign bits efficiently alongside INT3?
What is the effective compression ratio including per-channel RMS overhead? (FP16 D/head per layer-head)
